operations.title: Research state for no-three-in-line-77
operations.summary: The judge-established state comprises a verified 152-point no-three-in-line subset of G_76, the certified interval 152 ≤ D(77) ≤ 154, necessary occupancy conditions for hypothetical 153- and 154-point sets, and the unresolved exact value of D(77). No active adjudicative conflicts are present.

operations.title: Verified 152-point no-three-in-line subset of G_76
operations.summary: An exact computational certificate establishes a 152-point subset of G_76 with no three distinct collinear points. The verifier checks all 573,800 triples using exact integer determinants. It does not independently verify quarter-turn symmetry, but that limitation does not affect the certified no-three-in-line property. The encoded configuration is attributed to Achim Flammenkamp’s maintained database, while Robert is credited with reproducing and independently verifying the certificate; finer authorship history is undetermined.

operations.title: Certified interval for D(77)
operations.summary: The strongest supported current bound is 152 ≤ D(77) ≤ 154. The verified 152-point subset of G_76 supplies the lower bound by inclusion G_76 ⊂ G_77, while the capacity of at most two selected points on each of 77 rows supplies the upper bound.

operations.title: Near-capacity occupancy constraints in G_77
operations.summary: Any hypothetical 154-point no-three-in-line subset of G_77 must contain exactly two points in every row and column. Any hypothetical 153-point subset must contain two points in 76 rows and columns and one point in the remaining row and column. These are necessary conditions only and establish neither existence nor nonexistence.

operations.title: Exact value of D(77)
operations.summary: The exact value of D(77) remains unresolved within 152 ≤ D(77) ≤ 154. The supplied evidence provides neither a 153- or 154-point certificate nor an impossibility proof, symmetry-restricted negative result, or reproducible failed search narrowing those possibilities. This is an open mathematical question arising from missing evidence, not an adjudicative dispute.
